headline: India win eighth Women's Asia Cup title after crushing Sri Lanka
summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final at Dubai International Cricket Stadium, securing their record eighth title.
details: India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title, and fourth in the T20 format, by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.
Shafali Verma (68 off 39) and Smriti Mandhana (59 off 39) set a record opening stand of 129 runs, the highest partnership for any wicket in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.
This explosive start helped India post a formidable total of 183-5.
In response, Sri Lanka struggled to build momentum, eventually being bundled out for 111 despite India dropping five catches.
The Indian spin attack dominated the chase, with Shree Charani taking 4-20 and Deepti Sharma claiming 3-19.
Chamari Athapaththu top-scored for Sri Lanka with 36 runs. India now lead Sri Lanka 6-1 in Asia Cup final meetings.
caption:
A record-breaking opening stand and a lethal spin attack lead India to their 8th Women's Asia Cup title!

India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title, and fourth in the T20 format, by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.

Shafali Verma (68 off 39) and Smriti Mandhana (59 off 39) set a record opening stand of 129 runs, the highest partnership for any wicket in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.

This explosive start helped India post a formidable total of 183-5.

In response, Sri Lanka struggled to build momentum, eventually being bundled out for 111 despite India dropping five catches.

The Indian spin attack dominated the chase, with Shree Charani taking 4-20 and Deepti Sharma claiming 3-19.

Chamari Athapaththu top-scored for Sri Lanka with 36 runs. India now lead Sri Lanka 6-1 in Asia Cup final meetings.

headline_marked: 5 held as [[RAB busts gang selling govt data]] online
headline: 5 held as RAB busts gang selling govt data online
summary: The suspects allegedly traded NID, birth registration, and mobile banking records obtained from government servers.
details: The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested five people from across the country for allegedly selling citizens' personal information online.
The suspects are Abdus Salam Sarkar of Naogaon, Subrata Chandra Pal of Gazipur, Ismail Hossain Sohag of Noakhali, SM Nafi of Gopalganj, and Mehedi Hasan of Keraniganj.
According to RAB, Abdus Salam Sarkar launched an encrypted website called 'E Seba 24 Dot Top' in April to sell the stolen data.
Sarkar had previously worked as a temporary employee at the Election Commission between 2018 and 2022.
The gang allegedly traded NID and birth registration records, call detail records, mobile banking records, SIM ownership profiles, IMEI, and radio-location data.
While one suspect managed the website, the other four allegedly promoted the services on Facebook and took orders via WhatsApp.
RAB-2 Commander Additional DIG Naimul Hasan stated that the suspects provided accurate information in exchange for money by accessing government servers.
The authorities have stated that, so far, they have found no involvement of law-enforcement personnel in the data leak.
caption:
Your NID and birth registration data could have been for sale online.

The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested five people from across the country for allegedly selling citizens' personal information online.

The suspects are Abdus Salam Sarkar of Naogaon, Subrata Chandra Pal of Gazipur, Ismail Hossain Sohag of Noakhali, SM Nafi of Gopalganj, and Mehedi Hasan of Keraniganj.

According to RAB, Abdus Salam Sarkar launched an encrypted website called 'E Seba 24 Dot Top' in April to sell the stolen data.

Sarkar had previously worked as a temporary employee at the Election Commission between 2018 and 2022.

The gang allegedly traded NID and birth registration records, call detail records, mobile banking records, SIM ownership profiles, IMEI, and radio-location data.

While one suspect managed the website, the other four allegedly promoted the services on Facebook and took orders via WhatsApp.

RAB-2 Commander Additional DIG Naimul Hasan stated that the suspects provided accurate information in exchange for money by accessing government servers.

The authorities have stated that, so far, they have found no involvement of law-enforcement personnel in the data leak.
